title: Nazara Shares Fall 9% in a Week
content:
Nazara Technologies had the worst week of any Indian new-age tech stock, with its shares falling 9.13% in four trading days. The gaming company closed at ₹376.75 on BSE on 27 November, down from ₹414.60 a week earlier, according to the exchange’s own price history . That made it the biggest loser in Inc42’s weekly tracker of 69 new-age tech stocks, in a week when their combined value slipped 1.6%.

Almost all of the damage came in a single session on 25 November, when the stock dropped 7.8% on heavy volume. Nazara has made no announcement that explains the move, and its filings for the month cover only routine investor meetings. The fall also comes barely a month after the company reported the biggest quarter in its history.

The week started quietly, with Nazara slipping 1.2% to ₹409.55 on 23 November. There was no trading on 24 November, and the real move came the next day. Nazara opened at ₹408.35 on 25 November, fell as low as ₹372.90 and closed at ₹377.50, a drop of 7.8% in one session.

Trading volume shows how unusual that day was. Some 1,23,050 Nazara shares changed hands on BSE on 25 November, almost seven times the 18,009 traded on 23 November. The stock recovered slightly to ₹381.85 on 26 November, before closing the week at ₹376.75 on 27 November.

The slide followed a strong run earlier in the month. Nazara hit its 52-week high of ₹435.60 during trading on 17 November, so the week’s close leaves it about 13.5% below that peak. It is still about 74% above its 52-week low of ₹216, and BSE puts its market value at ₹14,493 crore.

Nazara’s BSE announcements for November contain nothing that would normally move the stock. The company filed notices of analyst and investor meetings on 13, 16, 20, 23 and 27 November, plus a monitoring agency report on 14 November for the quarter to 30 September. There were no results, deals, management changes or stake sales in the filings around 25 November.

title: LPL : grand ménage chez Weibo, Xiaohu seul rescapé pour 2027
content:
C’est la fin d’un projet qui n’aura jamais répondu aux attentes. Weibo Gaming a officialisé les départs de Zika, Xiaohao, Elk, Jwei et Moham, tous arrivés en fin de contrat le 17 novembre dernier. Le grand ménage s’est également étendu au coaching staff, avec les départs du head coach Clearlove et de ses deux adjoints, Shine et Tselin. Recrutés lors de la précédente intersaison, Zika et Elk quittent ainsi la structure après seulement une année.

Pourtant troisième du premier segment de la LPL en 2026, Weibo a progressivement sombré au fil de la saison, malgré de nombreux changements au sein de son effectif. Reléguée dans le Group Nirvana lors du Summer Split, l’équipe a terminé à une triste onzième place, sans même parvenir à se qualifier pour les playoffs. Un véritable fiasco pour les finalistes des Worlds 2023, qui n’ont disputé aucune compétition internationale cette année. Désormais libre, Elk serait notamment dans le viseur de JD Gaming et de Bilibili Gaming.

Selon les informations de la presse chinoise, Weibo Gaming aurait déjà bien avancé dans la construction de son effectif pour 2027. Seul rescapé du roster de 2026, Li « Xiaohu » Yuan-Hao devrait conserver sa place sur la midlane. Le vétéran chinois pourrait notamment retrouver son ancien coéquipier de Royal Never Give Up, Chen « GALA » Wei, en provenance de JD Gaming. Ce dernier serait associé à Erha, qui ferait son retour chez Weibo après un passage chez Team WE.

Pour son topside, la structure chinoise devrait se tourner vers la Corée du Sud en recrutant le duo de Ninjas in Pyjamas, composé du toplaner HOYA et du jungler Guwon. Avec quatre nouveaux titulaires autour de Xiaohu, Weibo espère ainsi retrouver les sommets de la LPL et renouer avec les compétitions internationales en 2027. Reste désormais à connaître l’identité du coaching staff chargé de diriger ce nouveau projet.

title: Astralis play FUT to end a five-year Major wait
content:
A win would take the Danes to the final Swiss stage of a Major for the first time since Stockholm 2021.

Few teams in Singapore have a less likely story than Astralis . In October they changed in-game leader, with Kamil “siuhy” Szkaradek taking over from HooXi . jabbi left on 16 November, and their fifth player, Anton “Anlelele” Huynh, is on loan from Sashi and says he got Staehr’s call about 30 minutes before the roster lock. After the first day of Stage 2, that lineup is 2-0.

Astralis face FUT Esports in a Bo3 on Sunday 11:30 CET with a place in Stage 3 of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 on the line. Both teams are 2-0 in Stage 2. The winner goes through 3-0, and the loser drops into the 2-1 pool and plays again on 30 November.

For Astralis, the prize is bigger than one more stage. The last time they reached the final Swiss stage before a Major’s playoffs was the Legends stage in Stockholm in 2021, which they reached by going 3-2 in the opening stage. Since then, they have missed five Majors in a row and gone out early at three others.

The 2025 format split the Major into three Swiss stages, so Stage 3 is the old Legends stage under a new name: the last 16 teams before the eight-team playoffs.

In Budapest, Liquid swept Astralis in the do-or-die 2-2 pool. In Cologne, they never got that far.

title: Fluxo’s Second World Title Puts Brazil Level With Thailand at the Top of Free Fire
content:
Fluxo W7M are the Free Fire world champions again. The Brazilian team won the FFWS 2026 Global Finals at BITEC LIVE in Bangkok on 28 November, two years after its first world title in Rio de Janeiro.

The win also changes the balance of power at the top of the competition. It is the fourth world title for a Brazilian team, which takes the country level with Thailand on the Free Fire World Series honours list. Free Fire Esports Brasil , Garena’s Brazilian esports account, celebrated by saying the trophy was going home to Brazil, while the champions poster names the roster as Butzin, Bops, MT7, Giuh and Proxx7.

O MUNDO É NOSSO. A HISTÓRIA É NOSSA. SOMOS BICAMPEÕES MUNDIAIS DE FREE FIRE SEGUE O FLUXO W7M! pic.twitter.com/t59CoLgJJp

The Grand Final used the Champion Rush format, so there was no fixed number of games in the 12-team lobby. Teams collected points for placement and eliminations, and a side that passed the points threshold could then take the title by winning a match. Garena’s post said Fluxo fought for every point “from the first drop to the final BOOYAH” on the way to the trophy.

Fluxo had to get past Buriram United Esports, the Thai side that beat it in last year’s final, as well as fellow Brazilians LOUD. LOUD won Game 4 with a Booyah, which the team confirmed on X at 12:35 UTC, as our Grand Final live updates recorded. After the title was decided, LOUD wrote on X that it had been one step away from conquering the world.

The other nine teams in the final were RRQ Kazu, Bigetron by Vitality, Resurrection Esports, Blue Cheese, All Gamers Global, GunDynasty, LYON, P Esports and Team Flash. Four of them came through the Last Chance stage on 27 November, while the rest qualified directly from the Knockout Stage. Garena had not posted a final points table or a tournament MVP when Fluxo lifted the trophy, so the size of the winning margin is not yet confirmed.

title: Fortnite announces ‘Special Treasure Hour’ on Dec. 5 before live event
content:
Fortnite has announced one final opportunity for players to acquire the Pirate Token and the other treasures available this season. This ‘Special Treasure Hour’ will take place on Dec. 5, preceding the season-ending live event.

If you are one of the many players still hunting for the Pirate Token, this could very well be the last stand. Here’s everything you need to know!

FINAL CHANCE "SPECIAL" TREASURE HOUR ANNOUNCED 🗓️ Dec 5th – 11am ET-1:20pm ET (2 hr 20m) "Hop aboard a special Treasure Hour from 11 AM to 1:20 PM ET, and the Out of Time event begins at 2 PM ET." pic.twitter.com/2wVCS5CD9P

Epic Games has announced that the Special Treasure Hour will take place on Saturday, Dec. 5, from 11 a.m. ET to 1:20 p.m. ET. This will take players right into the Out of Time live event, which is the Chapter 8 launch.

As for what sets this Treasure Hour apart from the previous ones , no one really knows. It’s safe to assume it will be worth attending if you’re one of the many players seeking a Gold skin or the Pirate Token .

This is the million-dollar question, but no one knows the answer yet. There have been rumors over the past few weeks that Epic Games would grant the Pirate Token to everyone before the season ends, but that remains unconfirmed.

title: FlyQuest need no jks heroics to sink PVISION in overtime
content:
INS, Vexite and nettik carried the load, and PVISION are one defeat from elimination.

FlyQuest beat PVISION 16-14 on Inferno after overtime in round two of Stage 2 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 , and did it with their Stage 1 talisman jks held to 11 kills. The Australians move to 1-1 after losing to FUT this morning. PVISION, beaten by NAVI earlier in the day, are 0-2.

The last round summed the match up: nettik took four kills and Vexite finished the job.

🔥 nettik's 4K helps FlyQuest upset PARIVISION once again! But can we even call it an upset if it's happened twice in less than a week? 😭 ( via @pglesports ) pic.twitter.com/o9GYJzOkLa

The teams met four days ago in Stage 1, and FlyQuest won 13-9 on Dust2 . PVISION made sure there was no repeat. They removed Nuke and then Dust2, FlyQuest took out Ancient, Mirage and Anubis, and PVISION’s Cache ban left Inferno. That was hardly a gift to PVISION: over the last three months FlyQuest had won 83% of their Inferno maps (18 played), PVISION 50% (12 played).

FlyQuest started on the CT side, and the early rounds belonged to the men facing Jame. Vexite beat the PVISION captain in a 1v1 to win the pistol round, then got the better of him again as FlyQuest went 4-0. aliStair , back with the AWP and the calls in this lineup, kept winning the duel between the two AWPing in-game leaders for most of the half.

title: LCS : Impact va rejoindre LYON… en tant que support !
content:
C’est l’une des grandes surprises de ce mercato en LCS. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Jeong « Impact » Eon-young (31 ans) aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec LYON pour la saison 2027. Après avoir exploré plusieurs pistes au poste de support, notamment celles menant à CoreJJ, Ackerman et Lehends, la structure mexicaine aurait finalement décidé de miser sur le vétéran sud-coréen pour remplacer Isles.

Si ce changement de poste peut surprendre, Impact avait justement débuté sa carrière professionnelle en tant que support chez Xenics Storm en 2012, avant de s’installer sur la toplane. Sacré champion du monde en 2013 avec SK Telecom T1, il avait rejoint l’Amérique du Nord en 2015, devenant au fil des années l’un des toplaners les plus titrés de l’histoire des LCS. Après une saison passée sous les couleurs de Sentinels, le vétéran s’apprête donc à retrouver son rôle de prédilection à ses débuts, près de quinze ans plus tard.

Avec l’arrivée d’Impact, LYON aurait désormais bouclé son recrutement. La structure mexicaine devrait également accueillir le jeune toplaner turc Kaan « Naak Nako » Okan, élu MVP de la saison régulière du Spring Split 2026 du LEC avec Vitality, pour les trois prochaines années. Le reste de l’effectif devrait rester inchangé, avec Inspired, Saint et Berserker, ce dernier ayant été élu MVP du Summer Split des LCS.

Le défi sera désormais de confirmer les excellents résultats obtenus en 2026, la meilleure saison de l’histoire de LYON sur League of Legends. Vainqueur du Lock-In et du Spring Split, troisième du MSI après avoir notamment balayé G2 Esports (3-0), puis quart de finaliste des Worlds, le club mexicain s’est imposé comme une référence en Amérique du Nord. Avec le recrutement de Naak Nako et le pari audacieux du repositionnement d’Impact, LYON entend bien poursuivre son ascension sur la scène internationale.

title: Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow DLC: Release Date, New Regions, Bosses, and More
content:
After nearly a year of vague “2026” promises, Team Cherry has finally announced a release date for Silksong’s first expansion. The highly anticipated DLC to Steam’s 2026 Game of the Year, Sea of Sorrow , is all set to launch next month, and existing players will be able to enjoy it for free.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Hollow Knight : Silksong Sea of Sorrow DLC ahead of its full release.

Team Cherry has officially confirmed that the Sea of Sorrow expansion will hit Hollow Knight: Silksong on December 11, 2026 . The date was revealed on November 27 during a short “Cherry Time” presentation, alongside a fresh trailer.

The expansion arrives on every platform the base game supports, including PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2. The expansion was first teased back in December 2025, which means players have waited roughly eleven months for specifics.

The footage shown in the initial presentation points to a major change of scenery coming with the Hollow Knight Silksong Sea of Sorrow expansion. The studio describes the expansion as a high-seas adventure with fresh areas to explore, and the trailer shows Hornet traveling across and beneath the water.

“In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves,” Team Cherry said in a statement . “We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong – crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses!”

title: Makeshift Astralis stun NAVI 13-11 after a 10-2 half
content:
Anlelele, called up half an hour before the roster lock, opened the round that saved it.

Astralis were not supposed to win this one. They came to Singapore with a borrowed fifth player and almost no time together, and they faced a NAVI side seventh in the VRS, 12 places above them, on a map NAVI had won eight times in 10 tries over the last three months. Astralis still beat them 13-11 on Ancient in round two of Stage 2 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 , and now sit 2-0, one win from Stage 3. NAVI drop to 1-1.

Astralis had a question for their followers once it was done.

How is your pick’ems going????? 2-0 😎 pic.twitter.com/jqtDNmjidw

The veto already looked like a gamble. Astralis removed Anubis, Mirage and Inferno, NAVI took out Dust2, Nuke and Cache, and Ancient was left: NAVI’s best map, and the one they had won 13-10 against PVISION a few hours earlier. NAVI had also won both maps when the teams last met, at PGL Cluj-Napoca in February.

None of that showed on Astralis’ T side. Anlelele finished b1t to win the pistol round, and Astralis ran to 5-0 before B1ad3 used a timeout. The damage was done in mid, where Staehr kept finding the flank through Red Room and ryu picked up whatever was left. In one round Staehr waited out NAVI’s rotation for two headshots and ryu then won the 1v2; ryu’s triple made it 9-2. makazze, who had run the same area this morning with 23 kills, finished on 10-19. siuhy mixed slow rounds with sudden hits on A, and NAVI never found a reply. It was 10-2 at the break.

title: LNZ’s three straight clutches drag MIBR past Imperial 16-14
content:
Imperial led 14-13 in overtime before MIBR’s Swedish captain won three rounds in a row as the last man standing.

Imperial had this map twice. They led 14-13 in overtime on Mirage, and they were 5v3 up in the final round. Both times LNZ found a way out, and three 1vX clutches in a row from the Swede gave MIBR a 16-14 win in a Brazilian derby between two 0-1 teams at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 (5-7, 7-5, overtime 4-2). MIBR, beaten 13-11 by 100 Thieves in the morning, are 1-1 in Stage 2. Imperial , who lost to Astralis earlier in the day, are 0-2, and one more defeat ends their Major.

MIBR were quick to count what the win was worth.

𝕺 𝖕𝖆𝖈𝖙𝖔 𝖊𝖘𝖙𝖆́ 𝖘𝖊𝖓𝖉𝖔 𝖋𝖊𝖎𝖙𝖔! 👻 Garantimos o 1-1 no primeiro dia do Major Singapore! Bora pra cima, amanhã tem mais uma madrugada sinistra. 💙 #MIBRCS2 #MAJOR pic.twitter.com/7pfCbXTzaO

The veto handed Imperial a map they like. They removed Ancient and Anubis, MIBR took out Dust2, Cache and Nuke, Imperial removed Inferno, and Mirage was left over. Over the last three months Imperial had won 69% of their 16 Mirage maps, MIBR half of their 12. The last time the two met, Imperial won a five-map series in the South American closed qualifier for PGL Bucharest in March.

VINI’s T side looked like it would settle it again. Imperial’s in-game leader kept his calls loose, with plenty of mid-round changes, and his team led 5-2 and 7-4. tomaszin, the Argentine on MIBR’s roster, kept the Brazilians in touch with one flank after another, and a run of three rounds forced Imperial to use two timeouts. nqz’s triple kill from catwalk made it 5-7 at the half.

title: LCS : le roster de Disguised au complet pour 2027
content:
Disguised passe enfin à l’action. Après s’être séparée de l’intégralité de son effectif à l’issue de la saison 2026, la structure de Disguised Toast aurait trouvé un accord avec quatre nouveaux joueurs, selon les informations de Sheep Esports . Le recrutement le plus notable serait celui de Juan Arturo « Contractz » Garcia (27 ans), qui devrait quitter Shopify Rebellion après deux saisons relativement décevantes.

[SOURCES] Contractz is set to join Disguised ahead of the 2027 #LCS season The 2023 LCS champion leaves Shopify Rebellion after two years and is set to be the first piece of Disguised's roster rebuild. Report by @LEC_Wooloo & @LCS_Eevee https://t.co/fokc9WHY5S

Champion des LCS en 2023 avec NRG et double quart de finaliste des Worlds (2017 et 2023), le jungler américain devrait apporter toute son expérience à un effectif particulièrement inexpérimenté. Il serait notamment associé à Kolby « PhyMini » Ashby (20 ans) sur la midlane. Véritable révélation du circuit nord-américain de deuxième division cette année, le jeune talent a terminé à deux reprises en tête de la saison régulière de la NACL avec NRG, avant de décrocher deux quatrièmes places en playoffs.

Pour compléter sa botlane, Disguised aurait décidé de se tourner vers l’Europe en recrutant Darius « Yakkey » Eduard Bistrian (21 ans). Passé par la NLC avant de rejoindre Vitality.Bee en cours de saison, l’ADC roumain n’a toutefois pas réussi à se qualifier pour les EMEA Masters cette année. Particulièrement performant en soloQ, avec un pic à 3 146 LP en Challenger en 2026, il s’apprête à découvrir le plus haut niveau de la compétition. Il devrait évoluer aux côtés d’Eric « Mixtsure » Yin (24 ans), ancien remplaçant de NRG ayant principalement évolué sur le circuit universitaire nord-américain.

Disguised aurait également bouclé son mercato avec la prolongation de Jett Michael « Srtty » Joye (24 ans). Arrivé au printemps dernier, le toplaner australo-américain serait ainsi le seul rescapé de l’effectif de 2026. La structure américaine mise une nouvelle fois sur des talents émergents pour tenter de bousculer la hiérarchie des LCS. Cinquième du premier segment en 2026, puis septième lors des deux suivants, Disguised n’a remporté que cinq de ses 19 séries disputées au cours de la saison. Toujours contrainte de défendre sa place dans l’élite en raison de son statut d’équipe invitée, l’organisation espère désormais franchir un cap sous l’impulsion de Contractz.

title: FUT turn 5-7 into 13-8 against 100 Thieves
content:
For the second time on Saturday, FUT trailed 5-7 on Cache at the break and won the map on their T side.

FUT Esports beat 100 Thieves 13-8 on Cache (5-7, 8-1) in the second round of Stage 2 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 , and they are 2-0, one win from Stage 3. It was the same shape as their morning, when they also went into half-time 5-7 down on Cache and took the last five rounds against FlyQuest . This time the second half finished 8-1. 100 Thieves, who had beaten MIBR 13-11 a few hours earlier, drop to 1-1.

FUT marked the result on X a few minutes after the last round.

Cache was what remained after the veto. 100 Thieves removed Mirage and Ancient, FUT took out Dust2, the map the Stage 1 survivors had built their run on, then Anubis and Inferno, and 100 Thieves’ Nuke ban left the map both teams had won on in the morning.

For 12 rounds, 100 Thieves looked the sharper side. Gizmy won the pistol round from the middle of the map, and although SunPayus finished off sirah with a Deagle to win the force buy that followed, the British in-game leader kept finding kills in mid and then turning back to rescue the round. His triple kill levelled the map at 3-3 in the middle of a six-round run, built on patient site hits and quick trades from rain and device . Gizmy had 13 kills at the break.

FUT stopped the run before half-time. They won an eco round with MP9s and pistols through mid, and in the last round of the half xfl0ud waited in a corner for two kills before dem0n won the final duel against rain for 5-7.

title: Ramayana Is Getting a ‘GTA-Style’ Video Game, Producer Namit Malhotra Reveals
content:
Namit Malhotra, the producer behind the Ramayana films, says a “GTA-style” video game based on the epic is in production. He made the comment on DD News, Doordarshan’s news channel, during an interview on Decode with Sudhir Chaudhary that aired on 27 November. Malhotra gave no studio, platform or release window, but he made it clear the game is part of a much bigger plan for the franchise.

The interview was broadcast in the same month that Ramayana: Part 1 reached cinemas, and Malhotra spent much of it on what comes next for the story. His comments about the game spread across social media on 28 November, a little over a week after Grand Theft Auto VI launched. DD News shared a clip from the conversation on X, with the full show on its YouTube channel .

#Decode | From Vision to Big Screen: Namit Malhotra's Ramayana Journey When Will the Next Chapter of Ramayana Arrive? Watch Full Show : https://t.co/ZdK2jJl1hR @sudhirchaudhary @malhotra_namit @WAVES_OTT #Decode #DecodeWithSudhirChaudhary #SudhirChaudhary #Ramayana … pic.twitter.com/kTVZofAX0p

The interview was in Hindi, and the lines below are the English versions carried by several outlets that reported it. “Even a GTA-type game is coming, but I will reveal more at the right time,” Malhotra said. He added that he wants every child to play Ramayana the way they play GTA, and to learn from it while they play.

He also gave a first idea of what players might do in the game. According to the same reports, Malhotra said players will be able to fly with Jatayu and fight with Ravana, and that this is what the team will show in a game that is already in production. Jatayu is the giant vulture who tries to rescue Sita from Ravana in the epic, so a flying sequence would fit the story closely.

Malhotra also pointed to the size of the games business, saying that the gaming industry has overtaken the film industry. He also spoke about theme parks, museums and animation built around the Ramayana. He did not explain what “GTA-style” means beyond those examples, so it is not yet clear whether the game will be open world.

title: How to Get the Rainbow Rolex Daytona in GTA 6
content:
The Rainbow Rolex Daytona in GTA 6 is a free luxury watch that players can pick up from a mansion on Casanova Island. Its in-game name is the Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’ (Sapphires & Gold). The island sits in the northeastern part of Vice City. Players do not need to finish Chapter 1 to reach it.

This guide explains the location, the steps to collect the watch, how to save it in the wardrobe, and what it adds to the 34 Luxury Watches collection.

The Rainbow Rolex Daytona is the Crowex Octane ‘Kaleidoscope’. It has a gold bracelet and a rainbow gemstone bezel. It has a gold chronograph with a rainbow sapphire bezel.

The watch is inside a mansion on the north side of Casanova Island. The island is in northeastern Vice City , near Vice Beach.

The mansion stands opposite the house that holds the Pegassi Toros, the game’s Lamborghini Urus. Inside, the watch is upstairs in the left bedroom, on the bedside table. The spot is a small table by a red chair.

You do not pay for the watch. You walk into the mansion and take it.

title: PUBG Gets Its Own Counter-Strike: 5v5 Demolition Mode Arrives on 2 December
content:
PUBG: Battlegrounds is getting a 5v5 round-based mode called Demolition, and it lands on PC on 2 December before reaching consoles on 10 December. The PUBG team calls it a new permanent Arcade mode, so it will stay in the game rather than rotate out after a short event. Its trailer shows a buy menu, two marked sites and a reactor to plant, which makes it unlike anything PUBG has run before.

The mode was first teased on 22 November as a permanent Arcade mode built for intense 5v5 attack-and-defend combat. A full trailer followed on 27 November, with a post on the official PUBG account setting out the main features and both launch dates. The dates are given in UTC, and the developers say every detail will be in the Update 44.2 patch notes on 1 December.

Every round counts. Every decision matters. Demolition brings a new competitive experience to PUBG with fast-paced 5v5 tactical combat, round-based weapon purchases, and skill-based matchmaking powered by a dedicated Demolition RP system. Battle across Hacienda and Paradise in… pic.twitter.com/CDfmxWG7h0

Demolition puts two teams of five against each other, with one side attacking and the other defending. In place of a bomb, the trailer shows attackers carrying a device called the Blue Zone Reactor and installing it at one of two marked sites, A or B. Defenders win a round by neutralising the reactor, and the on-screen messages in the trailer read “Blue Zone Reactor Installed” and “Blue Zone Reactor Neutralized”.

The trailer’s interface also fills in the structure of a match. The round counter reads “Round 1/13”, so a match can run to 13 rounds, and the official post confirms that the first team to win seven rounds takes it. A radial menu lets players mark Site A, Site B or the middle of the map, and attackers get an “Escort Reactor” call to rally teammates around the carrier. The gameplay clips that show the full interface are filmed in first person, although PUBG has not said whether a third-person option will exist.

Matches take place on two maps, Hacienda and Paradise. The names echo Hacienda del Patrón on Miramar and Paradise Resort on Sanhok, and the trailer shows sandy compounds, tiled roofs and palm trees, but PUBG has not yet published full layouts. The end of the trailer shows a 7 to 3 win, with a results screen that tracks how many reactors each team installed or dismantled.

title: Jorko finds 32 kills as Liquid outlast Eternal Fire 19-17
content:
Six kills against G2 in the morning, 32 on Anubis by lunchtime: the 17-year-old led the server as Liquid needed two overtimes.

Team Liquid are 1-1 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 after a 19-17 double-overtime win over Eternal Fire on Anubis, a result that leaves the Turkish side 0-2 and one defeat from elimination. A few hours earlier, in the 8-13 loss to G2 on Mirage, Jorko had managed six kills. Against Eternal Fire, Liquid’s AWPer finished 32-24 with 85.2 ADR, more kills than anyone else on the server.

Least stressful NA win pic.twitter.com/iDcasVrT7E

Eternal Fire removed Nuke, Inferno and Mirage, Liquid took out Ancient, Dust2 and Cache, and the two lineups met for the first time on the map that was left. Both had lost in the morning, Eternal Fire when nafany’s 28 kills carried THE ONE to a 13-10 win on Cache.

title: Where to Find Red Hulk in GTA 6: Kyle McKittrick’s Missions and Both Endings
content:
Red Hulk is Kyle McKittrick, and you meet him at McKittrick Farm in Frogswater, Kelly County, north-east of the Starlet Motel.

Start in Chapter 2 with the Pilot Wanted flyer at the Starlet Motel reception, then finish all three of Kyle’s Strangers & Freaks missions.

Helping the police take him down pays $5,000, while sparing him ends with a hug and no cash.

The Red Hulk in GTA 6 is Kyle McKittrick, a strawberry farmer in Kelly County whose chemical experiments go badly wrong. Finding him takes three side missions spread across Chapters 2 and 3, and the trail starts with a job advert pinned up at a roadside motel. Miss that advert and the whole storyline can pass you by, because nothing in the main story points you towards it.

Kyle became one of the most shared characters in Leonida soon after GTA 6 launched on 19 November . A clip from an IShowSpeed stream showed a huge red figure smashing out of a building, and players quickly nicknamed him Red Hulk. The clip below, shared on X that evening, shows the encounter most players are now trying to reach for themselves.

title: BELCHONOKK’s ace halts MongolZ fightback and puts THE ONE 2-0
content:
The MongolZ had won four rounds in a row to make it 11-8 on Mirage. BELCHONOKK, held to 11 kills in the morning, answered with an ace.

Hours after a quiet morning against Eternal Fire, BELCHONOKK picked the moment that mattered most. The MongolZ had clawed back from 4-11 to 8-11 on Mirage when he cleared all five of them on his own, and THE ONE closed out a 13-10 win two rounds later. It leaves them 2-0 in Stage 2 of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 , one win from Stage 3, while The MongolZ drop to 1-1.

THE ONE are still 1win everywhere else, but play this Major under a different name because of Singapore’s rules on gambling brands. In the morning their in-game leader nafany carried them past Eternal Fire with 28 kills on Cache , while BELCHONOKK finished on 11-17 with 54.7 ADR.

Against The MongolZ he looked like a different player. He came to THE ONE from PARIVISION, where he had been an anchor on the edge of the map. Here he plays the busiest CT position and opens rounds on the T side, and twice he won rounds almost on his own.

The first was the second pistol round. THE ONE lost a player early, yet BELCHONOKK stayed alive on A, did damage to three opponents without chasing kills, and froze The MongolZ until help arrived. The second came at 11-8. The MongolZ had won four rounds in a row on their CT side, and THE ONE had stopped closing out sites. BELCHONOKK held a dry angle towards window in mid, picked up kills there and on A ramp, then walked all the way round from T spawn to short on low health and finished cobrazera after the plant. Ace, and map point.

He ended on 17-18 with 94.8 ADR, second on his team only to Ax1Le.

title: Doubted AWPer r1nkle goes 24-10 as G2 top NIP 13-10
content:
Against the team where he made his name, r1nkle went 15-3 on the CT side and put G2 one win from Stage 3.

G2 are 2-0 in Stage 2 of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 after a 13-10 win over Ninjas in Pyjamas on Ancient, and the player who came into the event under the most pressure finished it with the cleanest numbers. r1nkle , who spent two years at NIP before his move to G2, went 24-10 with his AWP, while HeavyGod topped the server with 25 kills and 118.2 ADR. NIP had won all five of their maps in Singapore and six Bo1s in a row before this one.

Secret agent r1nkle strat didn't work. 1-1. GG @G2CSGO pic.twitter.com/a4iANsH2zE

The analysts spent part of the build-up picking at r1nkle: his AWP on Ancient had been a worry, and one of them called his move from NIP a disappointment. G2 removed Mirage, the map they had beaten Liquid on a few hours earlier, NIP took out Inferno and Dust2, and Ancient was left, a map NIP had been happy to play all event.

r1nkle’s first half settled the argument for one day at least. Playing on the CT side, he went 15-3, and early on he was eight kills up without a death. When NIP did get a bomb down, his repositioning and two late kills won the round back, and the casters were quick to point out who he was doing it against.

HeavyGod did the rest. He won the opening pistol round with the kills that kept it alive before NertZ finished it with his USP, and G2 went 4-0 up. NIP’s best answer came from stavn , who slipped into a smoke to catch NertZ and secured a plant with a double kill, but too many of their T rounds ended with players running through smokes into G2’s crossfire. One of those rounds came on a G2 eco and handed them a stack of free rifles. sAw called G2’s first timeout at 7-3, and the half finished 8-4.

title: KRAFTON India Awards 2026: All 18 Categories Revealed, Fan Voting Opens 7 December
content:
KRAFTON India has revealed the categories for the KRAFTON India Awards 2026, and fan voting opens on 7 December. The second edition has 18 awards across esports, creators, broadcast talent and community work, and four of the biggest esports awards will be decided purely by data, with no jury and no fan vote. KRAFTON India announced the list on Instagram with the campaign tag #CrownTheYear.

The ceremony is set for Goa in January 2027, as KRAFTON India confirmed during BMIC 2026 and as we set out in our report on the KRAFTON India Awards second edition in Goa . The judging is the biggest change from the first edition, with each category now carrying its own published mix of data, jury and fan votes.

The awards are split into five groups: Decided by Data, Esports, Creators, Talents and Honouring. Here is every category and how its winner will be chosen.

Esports Player, Esports Team, In-Game Leader and Emerging Star of the Year will all be decided by “verified KRAFTON India Esports season stats”, according to the announcement. KRAFTON India says these four will have “no jury” and “no vote”, which takes popularity out of the biggest competitive awards. The season data covers events such as BGIS, BMPS, BMSD and BMIC 2026, which also feed the KRAFTON India Esports rankings after BMIC 2026 .

The change answers one of the main complaints about the first edition, when fan voting played a big part in several esports categories. KRAFTON India has not yet published which stats it will use, such as finishes, damage, placements or titles, or how they will be weighted.

Most of the other categories use a 70% jury and 30% fan split. That covers the KIE Contributor award, all three creator awards and Caster of the Year, so fans can influence the result but cannot decide it alone. Host of the Year is the only category left entirely to fans.

title: Mandatory end Derke’s Kickoff hopes as MiniBoo beats big brother
content:
Three straight 2-1 defeats leave Aurora winless in the Europe Qualifier Playoffs and out of VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027.

Aurora Gaming are out of the race for VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027. Nikita “Derke” Sirmitev’s new team lost 2-1 to Mandatory on 27 November (Bind 14-16, Haven 13-9, Sunset 12-14), their third defeat in three series in the Swiss stage of the Europe Qualifier Playoffs. Three losses mean elimination, so Aurora finish the stage 0-3 with only xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx for company at the bottom.

The series that ended it was a family affair. Mandatory’s duelist Dominykas “MiniBoo” Lukaševičius is the younger brother of Aurora’s in-game leader Ričardas “Boo” Lukaševičius, and he finished 69-59 with 21 first kills across the three maps. Both of Mandatory’s map wins came in overtime, on their own Bind pick and in the Sunset decider.

Aurora were not short of firepower. Derke went 80-58 against Mandatory, the most kills of anyone on the server, and Nikita “trexx” Cherednichenko added 68-45. The problem was depth: Boo finished the series 37-58 and Vitaliy “B1SK” Emelyanov 46-56.

The pattern was the same every day. Against NAVI Junior on 25 November, Aurora took Bind 13-9 and then won only 11 rounds across Lotus and Haven. A day later they beat WIP Esports 13-9 on Sunset, lost their own Lotus pick 13-8 and were edged 14-12 in overtime on Haven. Mandatory then needed overtime twice to finish the job.

Aurora were only in the playoffs because of a second chance. BONK beat them 2-1 in Qualifier 1, but Riot threw BONK out of the qualifier on 8 November over cheating software and replayed the rounds after the Aurora series. Aurora used the reprieve to win Qualifier 1, beating Pixel Lumina 2-0 in the semi-final and F9 EICAR 2-1 in the grand final on 10 November (Lotus 11-13, Haven 13-7, Sunset 13-6). Riot later banned BONK’s five players and coach for four years .

title: How Team Soul Went Toe-to-Toe with the World’s Best in PMGC 2026 Gauntlet
content:
Team SouL showcased an impressive performance in PUBG Mobile 2026 Gauntlet stage to qualify for the highly prestigious Grand Final s. After the conclusion of the first day and six matches, Team SouL was in 11th position with a total 33 points. However, on the second day, the team showed a phenomenal performance and jumped to 6th position with 91 points.

Team SouL acquired 58 points on the second day alone, which makes the average of 9.67 points per match as compared to 5.5 points per match on the first day. Notably, the team secured 45 points in the last three matches, which were a spectacle to watch.

Going in, Team SouL was the fan favorite for every Indian fan, because they were representing the country. But honestly, nobody had any idea how they would actually do against their global counterparts. The Indian region is locked in its own bubble when it comes to PUBG Mobile competition. Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI), the India-specific variant of PUBG Mobile, does not have global matchmaking. So the only time Indian teams play international opposition is at the BGMI International Cup (BMIC), where we get to see South Korean and Japanese teams, or at a global PUBG Mobile event, which needs a dedicated Indian slot. Indian teams have only started getting those slots recently. Team SouL earned this one by winning the Battlegrounds Mobile India Showdown (BMSD) 2026 .

Before this, Orangutan, GodLike Esports, and True Rippers had represented India at global PUBG Mobile events. They did decently well. Orangutan and GodLike both made it to the PMWC 2026 Grand Finals in Paris, the first Indian teams ever to get that far. But none of them had shown this level of performance yet. Orangutan played the PMGC 2025 Gauntlet stage too but finished at 11th position, and then ended PMGC 2025 in 35th place, while True Rippers Esports finished at 36th position.

It’s only the start of the tournament, I know. Still, Team SouL has so far met the fans, the organization, and the supporters’ expectations. And it gets more impressive when you look at which teams they competed against.

S2G Esports won the PUBG Mobile World Cup (PMWC) 2026 in Paris. Wolves Esports won the PUBG Mobile Global Open (PMGO) 2026 Season 2 in Lahore. 4Thrives Esports won PMGO 2026 Season 1 in Jakarta. Nongshim RedForce won the PUBG Mobile Macao Invitational 2026. All Gamers won the Peacekeeper Elite League (PEL) Spring 2026.

title: Delaware Magistrate Orders Supermicro to Hand a Pension Fund Its Audit Minutes and a Grand Jury Subpoena
content:
A Delaware Court of Chancery magistrate has ruled that Super Micro Computer must hand a Chicago teachers’ pension fund more of its internal records, including Audit Committee minutes from December 2024. The ruling also covers, under strict conditions, a federal grand jury subpoena from New York linked to the export case against its co-founder. The findings are set out in a post-trial report by Magistrate Mitchell of the Court of Chancery, issued under seal on 17 November and published in redacted form on 25 November 2026. Either side can still challenge the report through exceptions before it is put into effect.

The plaintiff in case 2026-0615-LM is the Public School Teachers’ Pension and Retirement Fund of Chicago, and the defendant is Super Micro Computer. It is a books and records action, which means the fund asked to inspect company documents rather than suing anyone for damages. The report finds that the fund has a proper purpose for that inspection, but it states plainly that it does not establish wrongdoing by Supermicro or any of its directors.

The pension fund has held Supermicro shares since 2019 and sent its inspection demand on 7 February 2025, under Section 220 of the Delaware General Corporation Law . Supermicro turned down the demand but agreed to share documents under a confidentiality agreement, producing material between March 2025 and January 2026. The fund said key records were still missing, filed suit on 13 May 2026, and the court held a half-day trial on the papers on 17 September.

The fund asked for five more categories of documents, and dropped one interim report from its request at trial. The report grants four of the remaining requests in a limited form. Supermicro must produce the relevant parts of its Audit Committee minutes and agendas from meetings on 19 and 30 December 2024, which dealt with the auditor’s follow-up requests after the Special Committee’s report.

It must also produce existing material recording an oral interim presentation the Special Committee gave to auditor Ernst & Young on 2 October 2024, or informal records showing its substance if nothing formal exists. A third order covers supplemental findings the Special Committee shared with auditors in February 2025, including findings drawn from mobile devices, where the board or a committee considered them. In each case the order is limited to material the fund cannot already get from documents Supermicro has produced.

The most striking item is the grand jury subpoena. Supermicro confirmed at trial that a subpoena from the Southern District of New York exists, but argued it was discussed by the Special Committee rather than handed to it. The report found that the committee’s minutes and report refer to the subpoena without describing its scope, so it ordered production as long as no minutes or report describe that scope.

title: 100 Thieves hold off MIBR 13-11 as sirah finds his form
content:

100 Thieves go up 1-0 in Stage 2 as they defeat MIBR pic.twitter.com/07YsPxj1xn

100 Thieves were quicker to it. poiii’s triple kill and a double from device won the pistol round, and the first six rounds all went their way. sirah set the tone in round three, when the bomb could not be planted and he and rain still won a two-versus-four on B. 100 Thieves went into the break 8-4 up after a T half they will be happy with.

title: Take-Two Files Macca the Gator and Rockstar R* Music Trademarks in a Second Wave of GTA 6 Filings
content:
Take-Two Interactive filed 26 more US trademark applications on 29 and 30 October, starting the day after the 16 Vice City filings TalkEsport reported last month. The new batch includes the first applications for Macca the Gator, the cartoon alligator on Rockstar’s own GTA 6 merchandise, and a filing for the Rockstar R* logo on music recordings, CDs and vinyl. All 26 are listed under Take-Two Interactive Software in the US Patent and Trademark Office’s records, and none has been assigned to an examiner yet.

Most of the 28 October filings protected names such as Vice City and Vice City Leonida as plain words. Most of the new applications cover logos instead. Ten are for a stylised Vice City logo and five for a Vice City Leonida logo, while three cover a VI logo filled with palm trees and six cover the R* badge. The remaining two are word marks for Macca the Gator, filed on 29 October, three weeks before Grand Theft Auto VI launched on 19 November .

The first Macca the Gator application , serial number 50189569, covers toys, including action figures, collectible figures, plush toys, playing cards, puzzles and board games. The second application , serial number 50189508, covers shot glasses, drinking glasses, mugs, cocktail stirrers and decorative mirrors. Both were filed on an intent-to-use basis, which means Take-Two has not yet claimed that it sells goods under the name.

The filings themselves do not say what Macca the Gator is, but Rockstar’s store does. Its listing for The Goodtime State: Vice City Collection , a $399.99 box that does not include the game, describes the set as inspired by Leonida’s hit TV show, Macca the Gator. The box contains a Macca the Gator figure and a Macca the Gator magnetic mirror, and both item names carry a trademark symbol on the store page.

Those two items line up with the two applications, one covering toy figures and the other covering decorative mirrors. Rockstar first promoted the box in a Newswire post in September, and TalkEsport’s GTA 6 merch price list covers every item in it. The applications do not mention any other Macca products, and a trademark filing on its own is not an announcement of one.

The most unusual application in the batch is the R* music filing , serial number 50191187, which Take-Two filed on 30 October. It covers audio recordings featuring music, pre-recorded CDs, vinyl records and downloadable music files. The record describes the mark as a stylised R with a five-pointed star on its bottom right leg, enclosed in a square with rounded corners.

title: GameStop Pays $3.5 Million to End Lawsuit Over Ryan Cohen’s Withdrawn Billion Dollar Pay Award
content:
GameStop has agreed to pay $3.5 million to the lawyers behind a shareholder lawsuit that tried to block a vote on Ryan Cohen’s multibillion dollar stock option award. The company disclosed the payment in a Form 8-K filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 25 November 2026. The Delaware Court of Chancery dismissed the case a day earlier, on 24 November.

The money is described in the filing as a mootness fee, paid to the plaintiff’s counsel for attorneys’ fees, expenses and costs. GameStop says it agreed to the payment “without admitting any fault or wrongdoing” and in its business judgment. The filing also states that the court did not review the amount, and did not pass judgment on whether the fee was reasonable.

The disclosure sits under Item 8.01 of the report, the section headed “Other Events”. It is signed by Mark Robinson, GameStop’s general counsel and corporate secretary, and SEC records show it was accepted on the afternoon of 25 November. The report gives 24 November 2026 as the date of the earliest event it covers, which is the day the court signed off on the dismissal.

According to the filing, the court approved a stipulation and order dismissing all claims with prejudice as to the plaintiff. Claims by any other members of the proposed class were dismissed without prejudice, so the order does not shut them out. GameStop adds that the case will be closed once an affidavit confirming this disclosure has been filed with the court.

A mootness fee is paid when a company takes steps that make a lawsuit’s main demand unnecessary, and the plaintiff’s lawyers then seek payment for that result. In this case the steps came in June, when GameStop pulled Cohen’s award from the ballot and published extra information about a second proposal. The plaintiff withdrew its request for a temporary restraining order the next day, citing that supplement and “certain other agreements” made with the defendants.

The case was filed on 15 June 2026 as a proposed class action by The City of Pontiac Reestablished General Employees’ Retirement System, a public pension fund in Michigan. It named GameStop and all five of its directors, Ryan Cohen, Alan Attal, Larry Cheng, Jim Grube and Nathaniel Turner, under case number 2026-0785-JTL. The defendants deny any and all wrongdoing, according to the 8-K.

title: makazze rules Ancient’s mid as NAVI edge PVISION 13-10
content:
NAVI led 12-6 and needed a w0nderful clutch to finish. Their mid player won the map long before that.

Before a shot was fired, the analysts on the PGL broadcast said NAVI tend to live and die by makazze on Ancient, and that he had cooled off on the map this year. He answered with 23 kills, 103.9 ADR and a mid area PVISION could not get through. NAVI won 13-10 in their first match of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 , the same score as on Ancient when the teams met in Beijing three weeks ago. NAVI are 1-0 in Stage 2, PVISION 0-1.

First W is here! Another one today would be great! #navination #PGLMajor pic.twitter.com/1d9qkWyrgT

PVISION removed Nuke and Cache, NAVI took out Dust2, Anubis and Inferno, and Mirage went last, which left Ancient. On paper that suited NAVI, who had won seven of their nine Ancient maps in the last three months, but it is also the map PVISION play more than any other. Not everyone in the studio liked it. One analyst said before the start that he wished NAVI had banned it, because the mid fights on Ancient come down to who hits the flash first rather than step-by-step planning.

That is exactly where NAVI won it. makazze won eight of his ten direct duels around mid and kept PVISION playing a man or two down for most of the first half. NAVI raced to 5-0 before coach dastan used a timeout, and Aleksib found HObbit in the cave area in consecutive rounds as the CT side took shape.

iM finished 13-18, but his multi-kills came when NAVI needed them. The best was a triple with an MP9 that put the ninth round on the board.

title: nafany’s 28 kills make THE ONE’s Cache gamble pay
content:
THE ONE left Eternal Fire’s best map in the veto, saw a 10-5 lead become 10-10 and still won 13-10 behind their in-game leader.

THE ONE left Cache in the veto against Eternal Fire , a map the Turkish side had played 24 times in three months against their own five. For a spell late in the second half it looked like a mistake, as a 10-5 lead turned into 10-10. Their in-game leader nafany made sure it did not end that way. He finished 28-13 with 113.2 ADR, the most kills anyone has had on Cache at a CS2 Major, and THE ONE opened Stage 2 of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 with a 13-10 win.

The team plays under the 1win banner elsewhere, but Singapore’s rules on unlicensed gambling brands mean they are THE ONE at this Major .

Stage 2'nin nazarlığı deriz #modundayız | #forEF pic.twitter.com/dtUnr4ndou

THE ONE removed Ancient, Anubis and finally Nuke, and Eternal Fire took out Inferno, Mirage and Dust2. That left Cache, where Eternal Fire had won 67% of their 24 maps over the last three months. The one result that pointed THE ONE’s way was their 13-5 win over Spirit on the map at ESL Pro League in October.

THE ONE started on the T side and made the veto look clever. fame closed the pistol round with two headshots, and Ax1Le stopped Eternal Fire’s force buy with four kills. A switch to two AWPs on the CT side did not help Eternal Fire either, and it was 6-0 with regali and soulfly still waiting for their first kill.

title: NertZ haunts old team Liquid as G2 win 13-8
content:
G2 had won two of their previous 12 series. On a map Liquid had beaten them on in July, a 9-3 CT half put them 1-0.

G2 arrived in Singapore with two series wins from their previous 12 and a 15-day gap since their last match, a 1-2 defeat by Falcons at BLAST Rivals. Their first map at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 went 13-8 their way against Team Liquid on Mirage, and the G2 player with the best numbers had been on the other side earlier this year. NertZ , who moved from Liquid to G2 in the swap that sent malbsMd the other way, finished 19-12 with 89.5 ADR against his old team.

G2 removed Nuke, Cache and Anubis, Liquid took out Ancient, Dust2 and Inferno, and the map left over was the one Liquid had won 13-5 against the same G2 five at BLAST Bounty in July, on the way to a 2-0 series win. With G2’s three bans so predictable, Liquid more or less had the choice. G2 started on the CT side and turned it into a 9-3 half.

It could have opened very differently. Liquid won the first two duels of the pistol round, taking out r1nkle and huNter- , before MATYS saved it with three kills, the last in a long 1v1 against a wounded NAF , who tried to walk round the map to get behind him. G2 were 4-0 up soon after, NertZ finishing a retake with his pistol.

NertZ has arrived in Singapore Major 🔥 pic.twitter.com/iAcw5QQVOg

r1nkle had taken a beating from the analysts before the match over his AWP form. He answered with triple kills in back-to-back rounds, and G2 went 8-1 and then 9-1 up. EliGE was the one Liquid player who kept finding a way in: he won all five of his opening duels in the first half. JT, Liquid’s in-game leader, kept the half within reach when he won a clutch on the last round of it.

title: NVIDIA Taiwan Revenue Hits $30B, as Key Disclosure Vanishes
content:
Nvidia has stopped publishing its estimate of where the data centre hardware bought by its Taiwan-headquartered customers finally ends up, even as Taiwan has grown into more than a quarter of its revenue. The estimate put 86% of that revenue with end customers in the United States and Europe in the quarter to October 2025. It is missing from Nvidia’s quarterly reports for the three months to April and July 2026. Customers headquartered in Taiwan bought a record $30.30 billion in the quarter to 25 October 2026, according to the supplemental financial information Nvidia filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 17 November.

TalkEsport went through every quarterly and annual report Nvidia has filed since May 2024 to see how its Asian sales moved while Washington tightened chip exports. Besides the missing Taiwan estimate, two other shifts stand out in the company’s own figures. Revenue from China-headquartered customers collapsed and then recovered to $11.05 billion a quarter, and Singapore disappeared from the tables.

When Nvidia switched to counting revenue by customer headquarters in November 2025, it added a footnote estimating where the data centre products bought by Taiwan-headquartered customers finally ended up. For the quarter to October 2025, it estimated that 86% of that revenue was attributed to end customers in the United States and Europe. Its annual report for the year to January 2026 gave a figure of 76% for the full year.

That footnote was the only figure in Nvidia’s filings that followed the Taiwan money to its destination. The headquarters count shows who pays Nvidia, not where the hardware is installed, and Nvidia’s own filings warn that end customers and shipping locations can differ from a customer’s headquarters. Without the estimate, readers of the filings cannot tell how much of Nvidia’s Taiwan revenue ends up with customers outside the United States and Europe. That includes Asia and the Middle East, the regions at the centre of the US export debate.

That estimate does not appear in Nvidia’s quarterly reports for the three months to April and July 2026. It is also absent from the supplemental data for the quarter to October, and none of those documents explains why it was dropped. Over the same three quarters, Taiwan’s revenue rose from $12.01 billion to $30.30 billion, and its share of the total climbed from 15% to 26%. The question of where Nvidia hardware finally lands has already produced headlines this month, including Bloomberg’s report on restricted Blackwell hardware at a Shanghai data centre . Nvidia’s board has also set up a national security committee as Washington presses for answers on China chips.

The growth behind those numbers has been steady across both years. Taiwan-headquartered customers bought $6.19 billion in the quarter to October 2024 and $30.30 billion two years later, more than twice the $13.75 billion of a year earlier. In the first nine months of the current fiscal year they bought $69.29 billion, already well above the $42.35 billion recorded for the whole of the previous year.

title: Staehr and ryu lead new-look Astralis past Imperial 13-9
content:
Astralis played their first official match with Anlelele on a map Imperial left them. They led 9-3 at the half.

Nobody quite knew what to expect from Astralis in Singapore. They arrived with a stand-in, Anlelele on loan from Sashi , a month without a match and a five that had never played an official game together. Their answer was a 9-3 first half on Inferno and a 13-9 win over Imperial in their Stage 2 opener at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 . Astralis start 1-0. Imperial, who needed five matches to get out of Stage 1, are 0-1.

WWWWWWWW 🔥 1-0 against @imperialesports pic.twitter.com/9Bd7a7Eomw

Imperial spent their bans on Ancient, Dust2 and Cache, Astralis on Anubis, Mirage and Nuke, and Inferno was what was left. On paper it suited the Brazilians. Over the last three months Imperial had won 59% of their 17 Inferno maps, Astralis two of six, though those numbers belong to lineups with jabbi or cmtry in them, not this one. The team had flown in a couple of days early to give themselves a mini bootcamp, and it showed in a calm CT half.

ryu set the tone in the very first round, waiting for the bait to work and sweeping up the rest of the pistol. Astralis went 4-0 up, and Imperial coach tacitus had used two timeouts before round eight. Imperial’s T side kept running into the same problems: late executes, isolated entries and a player in chelo who went into half-time without a kill.

The pre-match talk on the broadcast was almost all about Staehr , and how many teams will want him once Singapore is over. He did nothing to cool that. On a second-half force buy he ran out of bullets and switched to his pistol for two more kills, and in the last round he took the first two duels on the way into the site. His 92.2 ADR was the highest on the server.

title: No weak link as NIP down Nemiga 13-7 on Mirage
content:
All five NIP players finished on 12 kills or more as an 8-4 T half held up against the Bucharest finalists.

Ninjas in Pyjamas came through Stage 1 without dropping a map, and they started Stage 2 of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 the same way. They won 13-7 against Nemiga on Mirage, their sixth Bo1 win in a row, and nobody on the team had to carry it. adamb and sjuush finished on 16 kills each, while stavn , at the bottom of NIP’s kill column, still went 12-7.

HAROSH start to Stage 2 😎 #PGLMajor pic.twitter.com/didofPLH2y

The two teams had never played each other before. NIP removed Anubis, Dust2 and Cache, Nemiga took out Inferno, Ancient and Nuke, and that left Mirage, a map Nemiga had won 70% of the time over the last three months against NIP’s 62%. Nemiga were slight favourites going in, and they had not played an official match since losing the PGL Masters Bucharest final to FURIA at the end of October.

Krimbo set the tone in the opening pistol round with four kills and a 1v2 to close it, and stavn landed the AWP shots that mattered as NIP went 3-0 up. KaiR0N- could have changed that early, but he missed a Galil shot at a player running up connector with his back turned. Nemiga hit back with a round won on two rifles and drew level at 3-3.

KRIMBO goes NUCLEAR on the T pistol 🔫 HUGE 4K and closes it out with the 1v2 clutch vs Nemiga ( via @pglesports ) pic.twitter.com/B12R5W5xVl

title: The MongolZ beat Lynn Vision 13-9 for a 14th straight map
content:
Lynn Vision got Inferno and a plan to go with it. The MongolZ won the duels, and have now won every map between the teams since 2023.

Lynn Vision got the map they would have picked and arrived with set plays for it. The MongolZ won Inferno 13-9 anyway to start Stage 2 of the PGL Major Singapore 2026 at 1-0. It is their 14th map in a row against Lynn Vision , whose last map win in the fixture came on Anubis in December 2023.

The MongolZ just CANNOT lose to Lynn Vision 😭 They win 13-9 to open Stage 2 and extend their head-to-head streak to 14 STRAIGHT maps. ( via @pglesports ) pic.twitter.com/evxFLNQIxO

The veto went Lynn Vision’s way. The MongolZ removed Anubis, Cache and Dust2, the map Lynn had won 80% of the time over three months, and after Lynn threw out Mirage, Ancient and Nuke, Inferno was left. Lynn had won 86% of their Inferno maps in that period. The MongolZ had won half of theirs, from 12 played.

Lynn Vision opened with a fake. Three players showed themselves at B without the bomb, The MongolZ rotated away, and C4LLM3SU3’s headshot opened up A for the pistol round. They converted, and later in the half they won a round from four against five on Desert Eagles and Tec-9s.

The MongolZ answered with individual quality. In their first gun round cobrazera held Banana alone and took four kills, and a few rounds later all five MongolZ players came down the middle together and won the round five against three. They still only led 7-5 at the half, with the casters crediting Lynn for how hard they had prepared.

title: FUT snap FlyQuest’s eight-match run with 13-10 comeback
content:
FlyQuest were 10-8 up after stealing rounds on light buys. FUT won the last five.

FUT Esports trailed FlyQuest 5-7 at the half and 8-10 late on, then took the last five rounds to win Cache 13-10 in their opening Stage 2 Bo1 at the PGL Major Singapore 2026 . It ends an eight-match winning run for the Australians, who came through Stage 1 at 3-0, and starts FUT’s Major at 1-0. FlyQuest go to 0-1.

FUT let their supporters know a few minutes after the last round.

you can't escape your fate pic.twitter.com/cnpjE0aEVW

Dust2 had been FlyQuest’s map all week. They won all three Stage 1 maps they played on it and 94% of their Dust2 maps over the last three months, and HLTV’s veto simulation had it as the most likely map to be played. FUT took it out with their first ban, out of pure respect, then removed Anubis and Inferno. FlyQuest threw out Ancient, Mirage and Nuke, which left Cache, a map FlyQuest had won 13-9 against Imperial on Wednesday and one FUT had played only three times in the last three months with this lineup.

The first half went FlyQuest’s way on rounds that looked lost. FUT had the pistol round under control early, and FlyQuest won it from two against five, with aliStair taking three kills. They later rushed B on a light buy with Tec-9s and took the site, which sent coach coolio to his first timeout, and late in the half they stole an eco round when nettik picked up an AK from a fallen FUT player and kept shooting. Most of their kills came from nettik and Vexite in the middle of the map.

title: 1 Million Subscribers, Zero Income: Onca Says YouTube Demonetised Every Channel It Runs
content:
Onca, an animation studio whose main YouTube channel has just passed one million subscribers, says YouTube has removed monetisation from every channel it runs. In a post on X on 28 November, the studio offered to trade its Gold Play Button for a five-minute conversation with a real person at YouTube. Onca says it pays 15 animators and has spent three weeks dealing with what it describes as a chatbot instead of a human.

Hey @YouTube , can I trade my Gold Play Button for 5-minute conversation with an actual human being? We just hit 1 MILLION subscribers, but instead of celebrating, we're fighting to save our entire business. YouTube approved our appeals, demonetized those same channels again… pic.twitter.com/giu87SoOWw

According to Onca’s statement, the trouble began months ago, when two older channels called Extremify and HardClipped were demonetised for reused content. The studio says it submitted video appeals showing its creative process, and YouTube approved both of them. Onca says it then stopped uploading to those channels and moved its time and money into new, original projects.

Both channels sat inactive for months, the studio says, before YouTube demonetised them again for the same reason. This time the action did not stop there, according to Onca. It says YouTube went on to remove monetisation from the channels it had built since, including its biggest channel, ONCA, as well as GAGA Global and James Films.

YOUTUBE WILL TAKE AWAY YOUR ENTIRE LIVELIHOOD OVERNIGHT. EVEN IF YOU FOLLOW THEIR OWN POLICIES. PLEASE read this until the end. What happened to us could happen to you, regardless of how successful you are. Months ago, two of our older YouTube channels were demonetized for… pic.twitter.com/nDZDcEOZY4

The channels involved are large by any measure. The ONCA YouTube channel showed 1.01 million subscribers and more than 1.58 billion total views on 28 November, across 236 videos. Most of its recent uploads are animated Shorts that retell viral real life stories, many with several million views each.

title: Jexen joins the JD Gaming coaching booth
Where Are the Virtus.pro Golden Five Now? pashaBiceps Runs an Energy Drink Brand as TaZ and NEO Coach at the Major
content:
Jarosław “pashaBiceps” Jarząbkowski is a Major champion, and these days he is also the chief executive of a snack and energy drink company. On 27 November, the Polish Counter-Strike legend told his followers on X that he has been selling his own products for almost two years, and that Papito Energy now ships across Europe. The post jokingly signed off from a “part-time businessman”, and it is a good moment to check in on the rest of the Virtus.pro line-up that fans still call the Golden Five.

Hello guys! Maybe you didn’t know, but I have my own products. It’s almost 2 years already. You can find some really tasty wafers, energy drinks with natural caffeine, they getting really great reviews. We now ship all over Europe, so you can order them and try it Who knows…… pic.twitter.com/Q9VHIWgKjy

The five Poles, pashaBiceps, Wiktor “TaZ” Wojtas, Filip “NEO” Kubski, Janusz “Snax” Pogorzelski and Paweł “byali” Bieliński, played together from late 2013 until early 2018. Their biggest night came in March 2014, when Virtus.pro won EMS One Katowice, the first Counter-Strike: Global Offensive Major held in Poland, by beating Ninjas in Pyjamas 2-0 in the grand final. The same core went on to win ELEAGUE Season 1 in 2016, and it stayed one of the most loved rosters in the game long after it split.

Papito Energy is based in Warsaw and sells its range through its own online shop at papitoenergy.com . The line-up includes energy drinks made with natural caffeine, energy gels, a wafer range called Fajny Wafel and clothing such as hoodies and oversized T-shirts. One of the drinks is named Lemon Mint Flashbang, and one shirt carries the line “What is your max ELO”, so the Counter-Strike roots are hard to miss.

The brand opened its X account in March 2025, and pasha now lists himself as its chief executive in his profile. He also runs Esport Ninja, which mixes esports with physical activity, and the Pasha Gaming Camp , which held esports and sports camps in Masuria in September and in the Tatra mountains in October. His joke about delivering orders on his bike is not a random one, either. In 2023 he cycled from Poland to Paris to follow 9INE at the BLAST Paris Major, as we covered in our report on his 1,000 mile ride .

Business has not replaced the community work that made him a fan favourite. In April 2026, pasha sold his Factory New Karambit Fade for more than $21,000 during a Polish charity stream and gave every cent to a children’s cancer charity, according to our story on the knife sale . He left Virtus.pro in February 2019 and has worked as a streamer and content creator ever since.

title: PARIVISION eliminates Aurora Gaming to stay alive at Dota 2 BLAST Slam 9
content:
PARIVISION players have kept their BLAST Slam 9 campaign alive after defeating Aurora Gaming in the lower-bracket quarterfinals. The CIS squad bounced back from its earlier surprising defeat to Team Liquid, winning 2-1 to eliminate Aurora Gaming and secure another shot at the tournament title.

With their victory against Aurora Gaming, PARIVISION players are set to face 1w Team, another squad that fell to Team Liquid earlier in the upper-bracket quarterfinals.

After suffering a one-sided defeat in Game 3 against Team Liquid, PARIVISION found themselves in a difficult position at BLAST Slam 9. This was an unexpected setback for one of the tournament’s strongest contenders, especially after the team finished at the top of Group C and secured a direct spot in the upper-bracket semifinals through the seeding matches.

Now forced to fight their way back into contention, PARIVISION must keep their championship hopes alive in a do-or-die series against Aurora Gaming in the playoffs , where another loss would bring its tournament run to an end.

PARIVISION started the series strongly, taking the opening game against Aurora Gaming, courtesy of Alan “Satanic” Gallyamov’s Sven, using his BKBs and God’s Strength wisely during teamfights.

However, Aurora refused to go down without a fight, delivering a comeback performance in Game 2 to force a deciding third map. Aurora Gaming’s hero lineup consisting of a Tiny-Queen of Pain combo paired with HP-sustaining offlane and support allowed them to quickly burst PARIVISION’s cores.

title: Ontario iGaming surpasses $10 billion in monthly wagers
content:
Ontario’s iGaming market hit a new monthly record of approximately $10.67 billion CAD in cash wagers.

According to data from iGaming Ontario, cash wagers reached $10.67 billion, a 15.3% year-on-year increase from October 2025’s $9.25 billion. Non-adjusted gross gaming revenue also reached $450.5 million, representing a 22.4% year-on-year increase and an 8% rise from September.

In terms of active player accounts, iGaming Ontario recorded 1.47 million in October, representing a 4% increase from September and a 14.2% year-on-year rise.

The online casino category remained the largest revenue contributor to Ontario’s iGaming market. In October 2026, that segment generated $360.5 million in gross gaming revenue, meaning another new record and a nearly 19% year-on-year increase.

Online casino wagers, meanwhile, reached $9.24 billion, accounting for 17% more compared to October 2025.

Sports betting recorded the strongest revenue growth among Ontario’s three regulated iGaming product categories. It had a 44.4% year-on-year increase and a 22% month-on-month increase. Meanwhile, cash waters went up 20% to reach a monthly record total of $1.29 billion.

title: « Gagner les Worlds plusieurs fois » : le rêve fou de Gentle Mates sur Rocket League
content:
C’est probablement l’équipe la plus attendue de la saison 2027 de Rocket League. Après avoir fait les beaux jours de Vitality et de la Karmine Corp, Alexis « zen » Bernier, Axel « Vatira » Touret et Tristan « Atow » Soyez ont décidé d’unir leurs forces chez Gentle Mates. « On était tous proches de la fin de nos contrats, donc on s’est dit que c’était le moment ou jamais de jouer ensemble » , a expliqué zen dans un entretien accordé à nos confrères de L’Équipe . Un choix également motivé par la volonté de former un effectif entièrement francophone. « Globalement, je pense qu’en Europe, on ne peut pas faire une meilleure équipe » , a même estimé Vatira.

Bien décidés à évoluer ensemble, les trois hommes auraient été prêts à se passer de structure si les négociations avec les clubs n’avaient pas abouti. Un feuilleton médiatique difficile à vivre pour les principaux intéressés, dont les familles ont également été prises pour cible sur les réseaux sociaux. Finalement, le choix de Gentle Mates répondait notamment à une volonté de repartir de zéro, sur un pied d’égalité. « On a eu des petits problèmes avec le club, qui ont joué. On est aussi partis du principe qu’on voulait tous partir sur un nouveau terrain. C’était important de ne pas avoir un joueur plus star qu’un autre. Donc M8 était le combo parfait, tout s’est aligné là-bas » , a expliqué Atow au sujet de son départ de la Karmine Corp.

Le roster est déjà foiré pic.twitter.com/YJBjq8A7sn

Déjà victorieux en Coupe de France à la mi-novembre, le trio ne compte évidemment pas s’arrêter en si bon chemin. Si zen a fait des championnats du monde sa grande priorité pour 2027, Vatira voit encore plus loin. « Évidemment, il faut gagner les Worlds une fois, mais notre objectif c’est de les gagner plusieurs fois, si possible, de laisser une trace, comme NRG ou G2 à l’époque. Notre rêve, c’est de performer sur plusieurs années et de gagner beaucoup de tournois. » Les trois joueurs entendent ainsi s’inscrire dans la durée, avec un projet pensé pour dominer la scène internationale pendant plusieurs saisons.

Au-delà de leur talent individuel, les trois joueurs sont convaincus de leur complémentarité. « Vatira, c’est le meilleur joueur du monde défensivement, je trouve. Zen, mécaniquement, il n’y a rien à dire. Moi, je suis un peu le joueur qui crée de l’espace, qui va faire le liant entre la défense et l’attaque. Sur le papier, on ne peut pas rêver mieux » , a détaillé Atow. Pour zen et Vatira, cette association représente aussi l’aboutissement d’une longue amitié, malgré la rivalité qui les opposait ces dernières années. « C’était l’icône de Vitality, moi de KC. Les gens nous assimilaient beaucoup à CR7 et Messi, par exemple. Mais j’avais aussi envie de voir ce que ça pouvait donner avec lui. Maintenant, c’est fait » , a conclu Vatira. Rendez-vous à Londres, du 9 au 13 décembre, pour les grands débuts internationaux de cette dream team.

Nos joueurs Rocket League pour la saison 2027 : @zenrll @Vatira5 @AtowRL pic.twitter.com/iaKTYbmyD0

title: Can Brazil Win a Fourth Free Fire World Title? Fluxo W7M and LOUD Lead the Charge in Bangkok
content:
Brazil goes into the FFWS 2026 Grand Final in Bangkok on 28 November chasing a fourth Free Fire world title, and it has two of the strongest teams in the lobby. Fluxo W7M, the 2024 world champions, and LOUD both qualified straight from the Knockout Stage, after the two sides topped the second matchday of Knockout Phase 2 together. They will face Buriram United Esports, the Thai side that beat Fluxo in last year’s final, in a 12-team lobby at BITEC LIVE.

Brazil had hoped to send a third team to the final, but LOS went out at the Last Chance stage on 27 November. Garena’s official standings show LOS finished fifth on 138 points, one point behind Bigetron by Vitality in fourth. RRQ Kazu, Bigetron by Vitality, Resurrection Esports and Blue Cheese took the last four places to complete the 12-team field. RRQ Kazu are a familiar rival, having finished three points behind Fluxo when a Brazilian team last won the world title in 2024.

No country has a longer record at the top of Free Fire than Brazil, and the numbers show how close it has come in the years it did not win. Corinthians won the first Free Fire World Series in Rio de Janeiro in 2019, and Magic Squad took the title in Bangkok in 2023. Fluxo added a third crown in front of a home crowd at Carioca Arena 1 in Rio in 2024, beating Indonesia’s RRQ Kazu by three points in the final stage.

The near misses are just as striking for a scene of Brazil’s size. LOUD finished second at the 2021 event in Singapore, Vivo Keyd Stats was runner-up in Bangkok in 2022, and Fluxo lost the 2025 final in Jakarta to Buriram United. That gives Brazilian teams a place in the final standings’ top two in six of the seven editions held since 2019.

Fluxo arrive as Brazil’s champions as well as its most recent world winners. The team won the second split of FFWS Brasil 2026 on 10 and 11 October with 198 points, four Booyahs and 105 eliminations across 13 matches, according to Brazilian coverage of the final. That result gave Fluxo W7M the last of Brazil’s three places in Bangkok, alongside LOUD and LOS.

LOUD finished second to Fluxo in that split with 185 points, after winning the first split of the Brazilian season earlier in the year, according to Brazilian Free Fire coverage. The organisation has a long history at this level, having finished second at the 2021 world final in Singapore. LOUD and Fluxo qualified for the Grand Final on the same day in Bangkok, taking the top two places in the Week 3 Day 2 lobby on 20 November.

title: FFWS 2026 Last Chance Results: RRQ Kazu, Bigetron, Resurrection and Blue Cheese Qualify as LOS Go Out
content:
RRQ Kazu, Bigetron by Vitality, Resurrection Esports and Blue Cheese took the last four places in the FFWS 2026 Grand Final after the Last Chance stage in Bangkok on 27 November. LOS, who finished second in Knockout Phase 1, went out after 10 matches at BITEC LIVE. That leaves Fluxo W7M and LOUD as Brazil’s only teams in the 12-team Grand Final on 28 November.

Garena confirmed the four qualifiers in its official Last Chance standings after the 10th match. RRQ Kazu topped the lobby on 161 points, ahead of Blue Cheese on 155, Resurrection Esports on 149 and Bigetron by Vitality on 139. Bigetron also posted on X that it had reached the Grand Final, and LOS confirmed its exit in a statement to fans.

Estamos fora da FFWS GLOBAL FINALS 2026. Não conseguimos encaixar o nosso game durante as 10 quedas e finalizamos a nossa participação na competição com aquele gostinho de que podíamos ter ido além. Encerramos a nossa temporada competitiva de 2026 no Free Fire com muito orgulho… pic.twitter.com/ZIP1T9Ivju

LOS came into the stage as one of the strongest names in the lobby. The Brazilian side finished second in Knockout Phase 1 with 636 points, but a poor third week of Knockout Phase 2 sent it to the Last Chance stage . Garena’s standings show LOS finished fifth on 138 points, a single point behind Bigetron in fourth.

The team did push hard late in the day. LOS won two Booyahs, a total bettered only by RRQ Kazu, and Garena’s Free Fire Esports Brasil account posted clips of the run during the broadcast. LOS finished with 84 eliminations, but its 54 placement points left it one point short of the top four.

In its statement, LOS said it never found its game over the 10 matches and felt it could have gone further. The organisation said it would close its 2026 Free Fire season proud of what it built during the year, and that it would carry the lessons into 2027. It also thanked its fans, who call themselves the Orange Wave.

title: HasanAbi Hits Back at OhnePixel Over GTA 6 Mandy Comments
content:
HasanAbi has hit back at CS2 streamer OhnePixel after OhnePixel criticised him over a collab with the voice actor behind GTA 6's viral NPC Mandy. The argument began this week, when Lexie Shoaibi joined Hasan's Twitch stream for a charity fundraiser. It adds a streamer feud to the noise around GTA 6, which has dominated streaming since launch.

HasanAbi has hit back at CS2 streamer OhnePixel after OhnePixel criticised him over a collab with the voice actor behind GTA 6's viral NPC Mandy. The argument began this week, when Lexie Shoaibi joined Hasan's Twitch stream for a charity fundraiser. It adds a streamer feud to the noise around GTA 6, which has dominated streaming since launch.

Lexie Shoaibi voices Mandy, the viral NPC in GTA 6. She appeared on HasanAbi's stream for a fundraiser supporting NILC and CHIRLA, two immigrant rights groups. Hasan said the two share a mutual friend and that he asked her to come on because she is a fan of his content.

A compilation of the stream went up on his YouTube channel. The video description is where he explained how the collab came about.

The next day, OhnePixel reacted to clips of the stream. He said he is not a fan of Hasan and that seeing Mandy's voice actor hang out with him leaves a sour taste. He added that hearing Mandy in the game now reminds him she is a big Hasan fan.

OhnePixel tied his dislike to a clip that went viral in late October 2025. It showed Hasan's dog Kaya yelping during a livestream and led to accusations that Hasan used a shock collar on her. Hasan has denied this. He has said the device was a vibration collar.
